distractorExplanations.c: Aspiration does not prevent nerve contact; paresthesia relates to needle trauma or the anesthetic agent.

prompt: Implant maintenance instrumentation should avoid

options.text: Plastic curets, which leave resin residue on the implant
Titanium curets, which are softer than the implant abutment
Stainless steel curets that scratch titanium surfaces
Glycine air polishing, which is too abrasive for titanium

explanation: Metal instruments can roughen implant surfaces and promote biofilm.

distractorExplanations.a: Plastic and resin instruments are recommended for implant maintenance because they do not scratch titanium.
distractorExplanations.b: Titanium curets match the implant's hardness and are recommended; they are not avoided.
distractorExplanations.d: Glycine powder is low-abrasive and is used around implants; it is not what should be avoided.

prompt: Desensitizing agents (e.g., potassium nitrate, fluoride) work by:

options.text: Increasing dentinal fluid flow so the pulp adapts to stimuli over time
Forming a resin bond layer the way a dentin bonding agent does
Occluding tubules or altering nerve excitability to reduce hypersensitivity
Sedating the pulp with anti-inflammatory action like eugenol

explanation: Sensitivity products block tubules or calm pulpal nerve response.

distractorExplanations.a: Under the hydrodynamic theory fluid movement causes the pain; desensitizers reduce flow rather than increase it.
distractorExplanations.b: Potassium nitrate and fluoride do not form a resin layer; that is how dentin bonding agents desensitize.
distractorExplanations.d: Eugenol is a sedative dressing material; potassium nitrate depolarizes nerve fibers and fluoride occludes tubules.

prompt: A treatment plan for gingivitis typically emphasizes

options.text: Biofilm control, professional debridement, and reevaluation
Scaling and root planing by quadrant with local anesthesia
Systemic antibiotics plus a chlorhexidine rinse for 6 months
Periodontal surgery referral when bleeding persists after one week

explanation: Gingivitis is reversible with plaque control and debridement.

distractorExplanations.b: Quadrant scaling and root planing treats periodontitis; gingivitis has no attachment loss to root plane.
distractorExplanations.c: Systemic antibiotics are not indicated for plaque-induced gingivitis, and long-term chlorhexidine stains teeth.
distractorExplanations.d: Gingivitis is reversible with biofilm control and debridement; surgery is not part of its treatment plan.

prompt: After nonsurgical periodontal therapy, reevaluation is typically scheduled to:

options.text: Take a full-mouth radiograph series to confirm new bone fill in the treated pockets
Repeat full-mouth scaling and root planing on a fixed schedule
Assess tissue response and residual pocketing for further care decisions
Polish the teeth and apply sealants before the maintenance phase starts

explanation: Reevaluation guides maintenance vs further therapy needs.

distractorExplanations.a: Bone fill is not expected or assessed radiographically at reevaluation; tissue response is measured clinically.
distractorExplanations.b: Further instrumentation is limited to residual sites identified at reevaluation, not repeated full-mouth on schedule.
distractorExplanations.d: Reevaluation exists to measure the periodontal response; polishing and sealants do not serve that purpose.

prompt: Periodontal maintenance intervals are commonly

options.text: Every 6 months, the same recall used for gingivitis patients
Individualized, often 3–4 months for periodontitis patients
Every 12 months once pockets have been reduced to 4 mm
Every 4–6 weeks for the first year after therapy

explanation: Risk-based maintenance (often 3–4 months) supports long-term stability.

distractorExplanations.a: A 6-month recall suits many healthy or gingivitis patients; treated periodontitis usually needs about 3-4 months.
distractorExplanations.c: Annual intervals are too long for treated periodontitis; pathogens repopulate pockets within about 3 months.
distractorExplanations.d: Four to six weeks is the timing of the reevaluation visit after therapy, not the ongoing maintenance interval.

prompt: Informed consent for periodontal therapy must include

options.text: The diagnosis and procedure codes, with risks given only if the patient asks
Risks, benefits, alternatives, and expected outcomes in understandable language
Risks and benefits in technical terms so the record is legally precise
A signed form listing the procedure, with any alternatives left for the dentist to discuss

explanation: Ethical/legal consent requires disclosure and voluntary agreement.

distractorExplanations.a: Material risks must be disclosed proactively; consent is not informed if risks wait for the patient to ask.
distractorExplanations.c: Consent requires language the patient understands; technical jargon undermines informed consent.
distractorExplanations.d: Alternatives, including no treatment, are a required element of the consent discussion, not an optional extra.

prompt: When evaluating sealant retention at recall, failure indicated by?

options.text: Slight wear on the occlusal surface of the sealant
Sealant discoloration without any marginal gap
A sealant that looks opaque white rather than clear
Partial/complete loss or catch with explorer

explanation: Lost or leaking sealants need repair to restore protection. Either finding indicates the need for repair or replacement.

distractorExplanations.a: Minor occlusal wear is expected; retention is judged by material loss or a marginal catch.
distractorExplanations.b: Surface staining with sealed margins is not retention failure; an explorer catch or loss is.
distractorExplanations.c: Many sealants are opaque white by design so they are easy to check; color is not a failure sign.

prompt: Cultural competence in dental hygiene care includes:

options.text: Adapting communication and care respectfully to patient cultural needs
Using family members as interpreters to save time and cost
Applying one standard script to every patient so that no cultural bias can enter care
Assuming a patient's beliefs from their ethnic background

explanation: Culturally responsive care improves understanding and outcomes.

distractorExplanations.b: Trained medical interpreters are preferred; family interpreters risk errors and privacy problems.

prompt: Evaluation of oral hygiene effectiveness is best done by:

Radiographic bone levels compared with the prior series

prompt: Success of periodontal therapy is best judged by:

options.text: Reduced BOP, improved attachment/probing trends, and controllable biofilm

Absence of patient-reported pain at the maintenance visit
Complete calculus removal at the visit, confirmed by careful tactile exploring
